title: Care Plan Updates and the Hand-Off Hold-Back on a Voided Prior Authorization
content:
**Care Management coordination bulletin — hand-off visits after a Prior Authorization void**

**Rule.** The hand-off hold-back of a void of a Prairie Ridge Prior Authorization approval looks at the member's active care management episode and the care plan updates recorded in the month before the day of the void:

- where the active episode is Complex Case Management or Health Home Services and at least one such update is recorded, 2 units are held back for the provider's hand-off visits;
- where the active episode is of any other tier and at least one such update is recorded, 1 unit is held back;
- otherwise nothing is held back for hand-off.

The hold-back is a whole number of units, taken once from the units the voided approval left unused; the units released are never below zero.

**Records read.** The member's Care Management episode active on the day of the void (its tier) and the care plan update activities recorded by its care team with an activity date in the month before that day. Care contacts, assessments and care-transition follow-ups are not care plan updates and do not count.

### Combinations

| Active episode tier | Care plan update in the month before the void | Hold-back |
|---|---|---|
| Complex Case Management | Yes | 2 units |
| Health Home Services | Yes | 2 units |
| Any other tier, such as LTSS Service Coordination | Yes | 1 unit |
| Any tier | No | Nothing |
| No active episode | — | Nothing |

### Hypothetical cases, for illustration only

- Active Complex Case Management episode with a care plan update two weeks before the void: **2 units**.
- Active Healthy Living Support episode with three care plan updates in the month: **1 unit**.
- Active Health Home Services episode whose latest care plan update is two months old: **nothing**.
